Fish:
Fish are vertebrates, animals with a backbone. They live in water and breathe with gills, which take dissolved oxygen from the water. Most fish have fins, scales, a streamlined body, and a heart with two chambers. They are ectothermic, so their body temperature follows the water.

Bony fish have a swim bladder to control floating and sinking, and a lateral line to sense movement. Fish are grouped into jawless fish, cartilaginous fish (sharks and rays) and bony fish. Most fish lay many eggs that are fertilized outside the body.
Amphibians:
Amphibians, such as frogs, toads and newts, live part of their life in water and part on land. They are ectothermic and have thin, moist skin without scales. Oxygen passes through the skin, so they must stay in damp places. The heart has three chambers.

Their eggs have no shell and are laid in water. Larvae called tadpoles breathe with gills. Through metamorphosis they grow legs and lungs and become adults. Amphibians are good indicators of pollution because their skin takes in harmful substances easily.
Reptiles:
Reptiles include lizards, snakes, turtles and crocodiles. They are ectothermic and control their temperature by basking in the sun or hiding in shade. Their dry skin is covered with scales that reduce water loss. They breathe with lungs all their lives, and most have a three-chamber heart. Crocodiles have four chambers.

Fertilization is internal. Most reptiles lay eggs with leathery shells on land, so they do not need water to reproduce. Because they do not use food energy to heat the body, reptiles need much less food than birds or mammals.
Birds:
Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates with feathers, wings, a beak without teeth, and a four-chamber heart. They keep a body temperature of about 40 to 42 °C, so they need much food energy. Fertilization is internal, and they lay hard-shelled eggs that parents keep warm.

Flight is helped by light hollow bones, strong chest muscles attached to the keel, streamlined feathers, and air sacs that give efficient breathing. Beak and foot shape match diet and habitat. Some birds, such as ostriches and penguins, cannot fly.
Mammals:
Mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates with hair or fur. Females have mammary glands and feed their young with milk. Mammals have a four-chamber heart, lungs, and a diaphragm for breathing. They have different kinds of teeth: incisors, canines and molars.

There are three groups. Monotremes lay eggs, marsupials carry small young in a pouch, and placental mammals develop young inside the mother's body, with a placenta. Whales, dolphins and bats are mammals, not fish or birds.
